body_text: 2026 Prom Tour Stops in Atlanta, New York, Knoxville, and Los Angeles Jan. 23, 2026 – Warner Bros. Discovery (Nasdaq: WBD) today announced the return of its hallmark student shopping experience, Say Yes to the Prom for 2026 , marking the program’s 14th year of helping students turn prom into a moment of confidence, creativity, and possibility . The multi-city prom tour will once again feature Monte Durham from TLC’S SAY YES TO THE DRESS: ATLANTA and employee volunteers from WBD offices in Atlanta, New York, Knoxville, and Los Angeles as they welcome 2,000 students for a full day of fashion and future-focused inspiration. Central to the flagship event is Macy’s , the program’s longtime and leading retail partner. Continuing its tradition of generosity and style leadership, Macy’s donated more than 2,000 trend-forward dresses, footwear, jewelry, and accessories, ensuring every student can express their personal style and shine bright on prom night. Throughout the signature shopping event students will get a chance to connect with WBD employees and receive resources highlighting mentorship, internship, and scholarship opportunities within the media and entertainment industry – equipping them with connections and tools to empower them in pursuit of their future career goals. Dates and locations for the 2026 Say Yes to the Prom Tour include: February 2–3 – Atlanta, GA, with affiliate partner Xfinity February 9–10 – Manhattan, NY, with affiliate partner Optimum March 2–3 – Knoxville, TN, with affiliate partner TDS March 11–12 – Los Angeles, CA, with affiliate partner DIRECTV “Over the past decade Say Yes to the Prom has evolved into a celebration of fashion and professional development for our youth,” said Dennis Williams, SVP of Corporate Social Responsibility for Warner Bros. Discovery. “The program in partnership with Macy’s will have supported nearly 10,000 students this year – some of whom went on to become WBD interns – and we are incredibly proud to continue this impact year after year.” “We are thrilled to continue our partnership with Warner Bros. Discovery to help deserving teenagers find the best look for such a meaningful moment in their lives,” said Sari Summers, buyer for young contemporary dresses at Macy’s. “Prom marks an important milestone and the perfect occasion to kick off Macy’s Year of Celebration.” Additional partners for this year’s prom tour include Men’s Wearhouse , providing custom tuxedo fittings and modern menswear rentals, and beauty leader L’Oréal , gifting cosmetics alongside onsite hair and makeup consultations from established CNN makeup artists. Companies contributing stylish finishing touches and other goods include Isaac Morris, Bee Darlin, City Studios, Sales One, Diff Eyewear, Jacmel, Bioworld and Hypnotic Hats. To learn more, please visit the Say Yes to the Prom website . Say Yes to the Prom is led in partnership with WBD’s Corporate Social Responsibility team, which is committed to positively impacting audiences and communities around the world and contributing to environmental solutions through our global impact initiatives. ### About Warner Bros. title: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals Announces NMPA Approval of REDEMPLO® (plozasiran) for Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome (FCS) in China
summary: - REDEMPLO is being launched in China by Sanofi - NMPA approval triggers $10 million milestone payment to be paid by Sanofi to Arrowhead subsidiary Visirna Therapeutics PASADENA, Calif. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jan. 7, 2026-- Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
body_text: - REDEMPLO is being launched in China by Sanofi - NMPA approval triggers $10 million milestone payment to be paid by Sanofi to Arrowhead subsidiary Visirna Therapeutics PASADENA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jan. 7, 2026-- Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARWR) today announced that the Chinese National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) has approved REDEMPLO ® (plozasiran) for the reduction of triglyceride levels in adult patients with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS). FCS is a severe, rare disease characterized by triglyceride levels that can be 10 to 100 times higher than normal leading to a substantially higher risk of developing acute, recurrent, and potentially fatal pancreatitis. REDEMPLO will be marketed in Greater China by Sanofi under an agreement between Sanofi and Arrowhead. In 2025, Sanofi purchased those rights from Visirna, a majority-owned subsidiary of Arrowhead created to develop and commercialize four of Arrowhead’s investigational cardiometabolic candidates in Greater China. Approval in China marks the third regulatory approval for REDEMPLO, following recent approvals by U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Health Canada, as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides in adults with FCS. REDEMPLO is also in review for marketing authorization by additional global regulatory authorities. REDEMPLO is the first and only U.S. FDA-approved, Health Canada-approved, and China NMPA-approved siRNA medicine for people living with FCS and can be self-administered at home with a simple subcutaneous injection once every three months. “NMPA approval of REDEMPLO for FCS in China is another positive step and continues the strong momentum since launching in the U.S. in November 2025. We look forward to working with Sanofi, an innovative global company with an established presence in China,” said Christopher Anzalone, Ph.D., President and CEO at Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals. “We are happy to report encouraging initial response from physicians and patients following FDA approval and launch in the U.S. last month. We intend to continue building on this rapid progress and anticipate additional commercial launches in 2026, pending regulatory review and approval.” About FCS Familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) is a severe and rare disease leading to extremely high triglyceride (TG) levels, typically over 880 mg/dL. Such severe elevations can lead to various serious signs and symptoms including acute and potentially fatal pancreatitis, chronic abdominal pain, diabetes, hepatic steatosis, and cognitive issues. Currently, there are limited therapeutic options to adequately treat FCS. About REDEMPLO® (plozasiran) REDEMPLO (plozasiran) is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Health Canada, and the Chinese National Medical Products Administration as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides for adults with Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome (FCS). REDEMPLO is an siRNA therapeutic designed to suppress the production of apoC-III, a protein produced in the liver that raises triglyceride levels by slowing their breakdown and clearance. By targeting apoC-III with sustained silencing, REDEMPLO delivers significant reductions in triglyceride levels. REDEMPLO is the first and only siRNA FDA-approved treatment studied in both genetically confirmed and clinically diagnosed patients living with FCS. For more information about REDEMPLO, visit Our Medicines . IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION CONTRAINDICATIONS None. ADVERSE REACTIONS Most common adverse reactions in REDEMPLO treated patients (incidence ≥10% of patients treated with REDEMPLO and >5% more frequently than with placebo) are hyperglycemia, headache, nausea, and injection site reaction. Please see full Prescribing Information for REDEMPLO®. About Plozasiran Plozasiran is a first-in-class investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutic designed to reduce production of apolipoprotein C-III (apoC-III) which is a component of triglyceride rich lipoproteins (TRLs) and a key regulator of triglyceride metabolism. ApoC-III increases triglyceride levels in the blood by inhibiting breakdown of TRLs by lipoprotein lipase and uptake of TRL remnants by hepatic receptors in the liver. The goal of treatment with plozasiran is to reduce the level of apoC-III, thereby reducing triglycerides and restoring lipids to more normal levels. In addition to the FDA approval of REDEMPLO as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides for adults with Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome, plozasiran has been submitted to additional global regulatory authorities for review and marketing authorization. Plozasiran is also being investigated in the SHASTA-3, SHASTA-4, and SHASTA-5 Phase 3 studies in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia and the MUIR Phase 3 study in patients with mixed hyperlipidemia. About Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals develops medicines that treat intractable diseases by silencing the genes that cause them. Using a broad portfolio of RNA chemistries and efficient modes of delivery, Arrowhead therapies trigger the RNA interference mechanism to induce rapid, deep, and durable knockdown of target genes. RNA interference, or RNAi, is a mechanism present in living cells that inhibits the expression of a specific gene, thereby affecting the production of a specific protein. Arrowhead’s RNAi-based therapeutics leverage this natural pathway of gene silencing. title: Complete Guide to AI Avatars: Types, Use Cases & Technologies
summary: An AI avatar is a digital representation or character powered by artificial intelligence technologies
body_text: What is an AI avatar? An AI avatar is a digital representation or character powered by artificial intelligence technologies. These avatars can be visualized as either static images, animated figures, or fully interactive digital beings that mimic human expressions, speech, and movements. AI avatars have become increasingly sophisticated, using modern generative AI technology to simulate lifelike presence and interactions in both virtual and real-world contexts. The use of AI avatars spans various industries, from entertainment to customer support and corporate training. They serve as virtual hosts, customer service agents, digital influencers, or even personalized assistants. At their core, AI avatars bridge the gap between human communication and digital interfaces, providing a dynamic, personalized, and scalable way to engage audiences and automate tasks that previously required human intervention. This is part of an extensive series of guides about AI technology . How do AI avatars work? Modern AI avatars function through the integration of several advanced technologies, each responsible for a different aspect of the avatar’s presence: visual representation, conversational ability, and behavioral realism. At the core is conversational AI , which handles how the avatar understands and responds to language. This builds on decades of natural language processing research, starting with early systems like ELIZA in the 1960s and evolving into today’s large language models, such as ChatGPT. These models process input text, generate relevant responses, and simulate human-like dialogue. To express these responses naturally, avatars use text-to-speech (TTS) systems. Advanced TTS models can produce speech with nuanced intonation, pacing, and emotional tone. This audio is then synchronized with the avatar’s visual output , which includes lip movements, facial expressions, and body gestures. This synchronization is powered by generative AI techniques like GANs and diffusion models, which can create photorealistic human faces and animate them in real time. Neural networks trained on large datasets of human behavior learn to map speech to matching visual cues, making avatars appear lifelike. The result is an AI-driven character that not only speaks but also gestures, blinks, and emotes as a real person would. Behind the scenes, machine learning models coordinate all of these components. They manage user interaction, interpret intent, generate responses, and render audio-visual output, all in near real time. The seamless integration of voice, face, and behavior creates the illusion of a sentient digital being. This layered architecture—language understanding, speech generation, and visual animation—is what enables AI avatars to interact naturally with users in video, chat, and immersive environments. Benefits of AI avatars AI avatars bring several practical and strategic advantages to organizations and individuals adopting them across various domains. By automating interaction and enhancing digital presence, they deliver both operational efficiency and improved user experience. 24/7 availability : AI avatars can operate continuously without fatigue, enabling around-the-clock support and engagement without the cost of shift-based human labor. Scalability : Once deployed, a single AI avatar can serve thousands of users simultaneously, making it highly scalable for customer service, training, or onboarding tasks. Cost efficiency : Reducing reliance on human agents lowers operational costs, particularly in roles that involve repetitive queries or high-volume communication. Consistency : AI avatars deliver uniform responses, reducing the risk of errors or variations in service quality that can occur with human agents. Multilingual support : Many AI avatars can process and respond in multiple languages, enabling companies to provide global customer support without hiring native speakers for each language. Personalization : By leveraging user data and behavior, AI avatars can tailor interactions to individual users, increasing relevance and engagement. Accessibility : AI avatars can interact through speech, text, or visual cues, helping users with different communication needs or disabilities. Training and simulation : In corporate learning or healthcare, AI avatars can simulate realistic scenarios, providing interactive and repeatable training environments. Brand representation : Custom-designed avatars can embody brand identity and values, serving as consistent and memorable touchpoints for users across platforms. Key types of AI avatars 2D vs. 3D Avatars 2D avatars are digital characters rendered in two dimensions, typically used in applications that require visual identity without complex animation. These avatars are commonly found in chatbots, web interfaces, and mobile apps, where graphical simplicity keeps computational requirements low. Despite being less immersive than 3D counterparts, 2D avatars can represent brands or users with custom designs, expression sets, and basic animations such as blinking, nodding, or simple gestures. 3D avatars add depth, perspective, and a higher degree of realism compared to 2D models. They simulate human or fantasy figures in a three-dimensional space, complete with articulated joints, muscles, facial features, and accessories. These avatars enable natural movements, body language, and environmental interaction within virtual or augmented reality environments, significantly improving immersion for applications like gaming, virtual meetings, and training simulations. Stock vs. custom avatars Stock avatars are pre-designed characters offered by avatar platforms with limited customization. They are fast to deploy and suitable for generic use cases like internal training, basic customer service, or demo applications. These avatars typically support a defined range of expressions, gestures, and voices, reducing development effort but also limiting brand differentiation. Custom avatars are tailor-made to match a specific identity, persona, or branding requirement. Typically created based on photos, videos, or audio provided by the user, they enable precise control over appearance, tone, behavior, and interactivity. While more resource-intensive to generate, custom avatars offer a unique digital presence aligned with company values or individual creators. Digital twin avatars Digital twin avatars are AI-generated replicas of real individuals, created using voice cloning, 3D modeling, and behavioral training data. These avatars mimic not only the physical appearance but also the communication style and personality traits of the person they represent. They are commonly used by executives, educators, or influencers to scale their presence across media, training, or customer engagements. Such avatars can deliver consistent messaging on behalf of their human counterparts, conduct interviews, or appear in video content without requiring the person to be physically present. While powerful for scale and personalization, digital twin avatars also raise ethical and legal considerations around consent, deepfakes, and identity management. Photorealistic vs. stylized avatars Photorealistic avatars strive to replicate actual human appearance and behavior, often using detailed 3D scanning, neural rendering, and shading techniques. These models can replace real actors in video content, power lifelike digital hosts, or stand in as realistic surrogates for remote collaboration. Achieving high photorealism increases trust and presence but also heightens the need for ethical use and privacy considerations. Stylized avatars purposely adopt cartoonish, exaggerated, or branded designs to evoke specific emotions and align with organizational identity. These avatars trade realism for audience appeal, often used in games, entertainment, and brand communications to attract specific demographics or fit unique creative visions. The choice between photorealistic and stylized approaches depends on the intended use case and audience expectations, with each offering distinct advantages and challenges. Primary use cases for AI avatars Marketing, advertising, and brand communication AI avatars are used in marketing systems as programmable digital representatives that deliver scripted and generative content across multiple channels. They integrate with content management systems, campaign tools, and analytics platforms to present consistent messaging while adapting language, visuals, and timing based on audience data. Example use cases: A consumer electronics brand deploys a virtual product expert on its website that explains features differently for first-time buyers and returning customers. A global retailer uses localized AI avatars with region-specific accents to present the same promotion across 12 markets. A SaaS company embeds an avatar in email landing pages to walk prospects through pricing tiers based on referral source. Corporate training and e-learning In training and e-learning environments, AI avatars act as delivery interfaces for structured instructional content and interactive simulations. They are connected to learning management systems and assessment engines, allowing them to present material, prompt learners, and respond to inputs in real time. Training flows can be adjusted dynamically based on performance data, completion rates, or learner responses. Example use cases: A logistics company uses an avatar-led simulation to train warehouse staff on updated safety procedures. A multinational enterprise deploys the same compliance training avatar across offices, with localized language and regulatory examples. A call center onboarding program uses an avatar to role-play customer scenarios and provide scripted feedback after each interaction. Sales enablement and product demos AI avatars are used in sales workflows as interactive presentation layers that guide prospects through products, configurations, and onboarding steps. They integrate with CRM systems and product databases to tailor explanations based on customer profile, industry, or stage in the funnel. This allows sales content to be delivered consistently while remaining context-aware. Example use cases: A B2B software vendor uses an avatar to demonstrate different platform modules depending on the visitor’s job title. An automotive manufacturer deploys avatars in virtual showrooms to explain trim options and financing models. A cybersecurity firm replaces recorded demo videos with an avatar that answers common technical questions during live presentations. Customer support and conversational interfaces In customer support systems, AI avatars function as visual interfaces layered on top of conversational AI and backend service logic. They connect to ticketing systems, knowledge bases, and account data to guide users through troubleshooting steps or service processes. The avatar provides visual and verbal confirmation of actions, reducing ambiguity in multi-step interactions. Example use cases: A telecom provider uses an avatar to guide customers through router setup while verifying account details. A banking app deploys an avatar to explain transaction statuses and escalate exceptions to human agents. An insurance platform uses an avatar to walk users through claim submission while validating uploaded documents. Media, entertainment, and creator economy In media and creator workflows, AI avatars are used as reusable digital performers that generate video, audio, and interactive content. They are driven by scripts, prompts, or live inputs and can be rendered across formats without physical production constraints. This enables rapid content iteration while keeping the visual identity consistent. Example use cases: A financial news publisher uses an avatar anchor to generate short daily market updates from structured data feeds. A gaming streamer operates an avatar persona that reacts to chat messages during live broadcasts. An online educator creates a branded avatar host to deliver course updates, announcements, and Q&A sessions. Core AI technologies behind modern AI avatars Face tracking and landmark detection models Face tracking uses computer vision to locate and follow a person’s face and key facial features (eyes, nose, mouth) frame-by-frame in video or live streams. These systems rely on deep learning models trained to detect and predict facial landmarks, which are precise points on the face that define its structure and expressions. Landmark detection outputs sets of coordinates for these points, enabling realistic animation of expressions and head movement when driving an avatar. Technologies like Google’s MediaPipe face landmarker work in real time and provide 3D landmark outputs and expression coefficients that help animate avatars naturally. Diffusion and generative video models Diffusion models are a class of generative AI that create or edit images and videos by gradually denoising random inputs into coherent visual content. Recent advances include models capable of synthesizing high-quality videos, editing motion, or animating characters — forming the visual backbone of photorealistic avatar generation. In research, diffusion frameworks guided by facial landmarks or audio cues enable synchronized talking faces and expressive motion in avatar videos. These systems support both text-to-video and motion-aware generation, and are being rapidly expanded across open-source and commercial toolkits. Text-to-speech and voice cloning systems Text-to-speech (TTS) systems convert text input into natural-sounding spoken audio. Modern TTS models use neural networks to produce expressive speech with realistic intonation, pacing, and emotion. Voice cloning extends TTS by creating synthetic voices that mimic specific individuals’ vocal characteristics from recordings, enabling personalized or branded avatar speech. These technologies can be tightly integrated with avatars so their audio output matches lip movement and emotional cues. Gesture, expression, and emotion synthesis This technology synthesizes the non-verbal behavior of avatars, including facial expressions, gestures, and emotional states. AI models learn mappings from speech, intent, or detected emotion to coordinated animations: lip sync aligned to phonemes, eyebrow and eye motion matching sentiment, and body gestures that reflect communicative intent. Tools like NVIDIA’s Audio2Face analyze audio to predict facial motion and emotional cues, driving lifelike expression without external sensors, while research projects aim to produce synchronized talking-face video that preserves expressive detail throughout. Key considerations for selecting an AI avatar tool Before choosing an AI avatar platform, it’s essential to evaluate key factors that affect implementation, performance, and long-term usability. Here are the primary considerations: Use case alignment : Determine whether the tool supports your intended application—be it customer support, training, content creation, or marketing. Some platforms specialize in real-time interactivity, while others focus on video generation or avatar customization. Avatar types and quality : Evaluate whether the platform offers 2D, 3D, talking, or photorealistic avatars, and assess the realism and animation fidelity. Ensure the available styles align with your brand identity and audience expectations. Input and output modalities : Check the types of user inputs (text, voice, video) the tool can process and the output formats it generates. This affects compatibility with existing workflows, devices, and deployment environments. Customization options : Look for tools that allow branding, personality tuning, voice selection, and multilingual support. The ability to control visual and behavioral characteristics is critical for user engagement and brand consistency. Integration capabilities : Assess how easily the avatar system integrates with your current platforms, such as CRM, LMS, or CMS, via APIs or SDKs. Seamless integration enables smoother deployment and richer user experiences. Latency and performance : For real-time applications, low latency is crucial. Evaluate performance benchmarks, especially if avatars are expected to operate on mobile or edge devices with limited compute resources. Security and privacy : Confirm that the platform complies with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) and supports secure data handling, especially if avatars access sensitive or personal information. Pricing and licensing : Analyze pricing models, such as subscription, usage-based, or per-seat—and ensure the total cost aligns with your budget and expected scale. Consider long-term commitments and hidden costs. They operate as conversational, context-aware video agents that listen, see, and adapt in the moment, guiding every user toward clear outcomes, whether resolving a support issue, completing onboarding, or exploring content. As part of Kaltura’s AI Experience Cloud, these avatars plug directly into your existing video, knowledge, and communication ecosystems, instantly turning your content into a continuously available expert. Leading organizations across technology, financial services, healthcare and pharma, IT and professional services, retail and manufacturing, education and public sector, and media and telecom already rely on Kaltura to power mission-critical experiences at scale. Kaltura’s avatars are engineered for outcomes, not just interactions: they reach around 95% accuracy in understanding user queries, handle over one million interactions each month, and stay available 24/7 for continuous engagement. title: Stacker vs Airtable: Which is Better in January 2026?
summary: Compare Stacker vs Airtable in January 2026. Learn which platform is better for building custom business apps, client portals, and managing external users.
body_text: If you're comparing Airtable vs Stacker , you've probably hit the point where organizing your data isn't enough anymore. Airtable does a solid job as a relational database with a friendly interface, but when you need to build client portals, create department-specific views, or give external users limited access without exposing your entire workspace, you'll find yourself fighting how it’s set up. The decision is less about ticking off features and more about whether you’re maintaining a database or running business software that people outside your core team can actually use. TLDR: Stacker builds custom business apps with AI and role-based access; Airtable is mainly a database tool. Airtable struggles with external user portals and custom workflows once you move beyond spreadsheet views.​ Stacker shines for client and vendor portals with granular permissions Airtable can’t easily match. Airtable’s pricing rises quickly as you add external users; Stacker offers better value when many people need limited access. Stacker turns your data into structured apps; Airtable keeps you in a grid-centric experience. What is Airtable? Airtable is a spreadsheet–database hybrid that lets teams store, relate, and view data in a flexible grid, which sits right in the middle of the classic database vs. spreadsheet . You can create tables, link records, and see information in Grid, Kanban, Calendar, or Gantt views, which makes it popular for shared project lists, content calendars, and lightweight tracking systems. It also includes Interface Designer and basic automation so you can layer simple “apps” and workflows on top of your bases.​ In practice, Airtable works best when your team lives inside the tool and is happy working with tables and views. It’s an upgrade from traditional spreadsheets, but it’s still built around the idea that your main users are internal collaborators looking at rows and fields. What is Stacker? Stacker is a no-code tool (with integrated AI) that lets non-technical teams build custom apps, such as CRMs, internal tools, and secure portals, on top of a built-in relational database or on data from Airtable, Google Sheets, and other sources. You describe the app you want in plain English, and Stacker’s AI builder generates a working version you can immediately refine in a visual editor. From there, you add pages, lists, forms, and dashboards for different audiences, while fine-tuning role-based permissions so internal staff, customers, and partners each see only what they should. Typical uses include flexible CRMs, work trackers, process pipelines, inventory tools, and client or vendor portals for niche industries where off-the-shelf software doesn’t fit. Data Architecture and Day-to-Day Use When looking at Stacker vs Airtable, the key difference is how each tool thinks about data and everyday work. Both store information, but only one is built to be the “front door” your team and external users use daily. Airtable Airtable works as a relational database with a spreadsheet interface. You define tables, link them, and then build different views to slice the same data: one base might power a content calendar, asset library, and simple production tracker all at once. This is ideal if your main focus is collecting and structuring data and your team is comfortable jumping between views inside a single workspace.​ However, the experience is still data-first. Interfaces and apps stay tightly coupled to the underlying tables, and most users end up working with a grid or grid-like layout. That’s why many teams start looking at Airtable alternatives for business apps once they need richer workflows or external-facing experiences. Stacker Stacker treats the database as a stable system of record and then layers purpose-built applications on top. You can use Stacker’s own relational tables or sync from Airtable and Google Sheets, but in all cases the goal is the same: give each audience a clean, task-focused view, not a generic table. For example, the same dataset can power: A sales pipeline view for your team. A minimal portal view where each client sees their own deals and documents. An internal dashboard for leadership with rolled-up metrics. Because these interfaces sit on a managed no-code layer, you’re free to reshape layouts and flows without breaking your underlying data. External User Access and Portal Capabilities If you need clients, vendors, or partners logging into your system, the contrast between Airtable and Stacker becomes very clear. Airtable Airtable was designed around internal collaborators sharing bases. External access is possible, but you typically pay per user and work around the fact that interfaces are built for people who understand the underlying structure. Dedicated portal solutions on top of Airtable often cost about 120–150 dollars per month for roughly 15 seats, which adds up quickly when you have many clients.​ You can share read-only views or basic interfaces, but fine-grained control such as “each customer only sees their projects and tickets” is difficult to implement cleanly at scale, and pricing becomes a bottleneck.​ Stacker Stacker was built with portals and multi-audience apps in mind. You can: Create login experiences for customers, vendors, and partners. Use field- and record-level permissions so each external user only sees their own records. Run internal and external experiences from the same app, without duplicating data. Because external access is a core scenario, Stacker’s pricing and permission model make it realistic to invite many outside users without blowing up your budget. This is why Stacker often appears in lists of best no-code customer portal tools and client portal software. Customization and Application Flexibility This section is about how far you can push each tool from “nice database” into “tailored app your team and customers enjoy using. Airtable Airtable’s strengths sit firmly in data organization: you can choose from Grid, Kanban, Gantt, Calendar, and Gallery views and apply filters, grouping, and color-coding to match internal needs. For teams that are happy working inside a data tool, that might be enough.​ But tailoring Airtable for more complex use cases, such as a full flexible CRM or a deep partner portal, exposes some gaps: Interfaces still reflect your underlying tables versus each audience’s ideal workflow. You have limited control over how different roles experience the same process. Extending the system often means more bases, more views, and more sharing rules to maintain.Pricing and Scalability for Growing Teams Using Custom Business Application Builders Stacker Stacker is designed to let you shape the experience around your process. You can: Use the AI builder to get a starting app from a short prompt, then refine it. Adjust each page and list so different roles see different actions, fields, and layouts. Add computed fields, status pipelines, and basic automations to guide records through clear steps. In practice, a marketing request tracker, a post-sale onboarding pipeline, and a vendor work assignment portal can all live in one Stacker app, each with its own interface but shared data underneath. Final Thoughts on Stacker or Airtable for Your Business The Stacker or Airtable question really comes down to how you want people to interact with your data over the next year or two. If you’re ready to offer logins to clients and partners, control what each role sees, and run core processes in one shared app, Stacker is likely the better fit for 2026. If you need to build applications with custom workflows, external user access, or client and vendor portals, Stacker fits better because it’s designed for running business apps instead of just managing tables. title: Does your ADHD brain feel numb?
summary: Learn what anhedonia means for ADHD brains, and discover gentle ways to reconnect with activities you used to love.
body_text: You know that feeling when your favorite video game sits untouched for weeks? Or when your craft supplies gather dust even though creating used to light you up inside? If you've ever felt like the joy has been sucked out of activities you used to love, you're not alone. This experience has a name: anhedonia. (And yes, it's totally normal if you just thought "an-he- what -ia?" Let's break it down together.) Anhedonia is the reduced ability to feel pleasure or enjoyment from activities. It’s one of the most common symptoms of depression, but it can also go along with several other mental health conditions - like ADHD, Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), and bipolar disorder - or even occur on its own. Think of it like someone turned down the volume knob on your happiness levels. And for those of us with ADHD, it can show up more often than we might realize. ☹️ What makes anhedonia more common in ADHD brains? Let's talk about what's happening in our brains when anhedonia shows up. There's an area of the brain called the ventral striatum (it sits above and behind your ears) that acts like our internal joy processor. In individuals with ADHD, this area is less active than it should be, especially when anticipating a reward. This decreased activity in the ventral striatum in ADHD is also seen in people experiencing anhedonia. The ventral striatum also works with two important brain chemicals: dopamine and serotonin. Dopamine is our "feel-good" chemical. It helps us get excited about rewards. Serotonin helps regulate our sleep, mood, and even digestion. Studies have shown that: Dopamine functioning is altered in people with ADHD, which disrupts the brain’s reward system. There’s less dopamine to go around - possibly due to a gene called DRD2, which tells the brain how much dopamine to release. The lower the dopamine, the harder it is to feel motivated. When serotonin levels are off, as they tend to be in depression, it can block dopamine from doing its job properly in the ventral striatum. 😮💨 What’s the difference between anhedonia and apathy? Sometimes people mix up anhedonia (not feeling pleasure) with apathy (not feeling motivated). While they often show up together, they're actually different things. It’s not just a semantic difference, either; differentiating between the two is important, because the strategies that help with each are different. Think of it this way: with anhedonia, you might want to play your favorite game but it just doesn't feel fun. With apathy, you might know the game is fun but can't find the energy to start playing. Understanding which one you're dealing with (or if it's both) can help you find the right support. For example, if it's mainly anhedonia, you might need help reconnecting with pleasure. If it's mainly apathy, you might need help with motivation and energy. 📋What are the signs and symptoms of anhedonia? Anhedonia shows up in two main ways: Social anhedonia : When being around people doesn't bring the usual warmth or connection. Maybe you've been dodging friend hangouts or family calls because they just feel... meh. Physical anhedonia : When physical sensations lose their spark. Food might taste bland, your favorite music might feel flat, or physical touch might not give you the comfort it usually does. A few symptoms of anhedonia to look out for: Activities you normally love feel more like items on a to-do list Winning or succeeding at something doesn't give you that happy buzz Food doesn't taste as flavorful as it usually does Your favorite shows or games feel boring Spending time with friends feels draining instead of energizing Withdrawing from or avoiding social activities much more than usual Music doesn't hit the same way it used to You tend to speak in a flat, monotone voice with little emotion Loss of libido (interest in sex) and/or pleasure from sex Physical discomfort or pain Turning to substances to try to feel more Trouble keeping up with bills or work 🔋How do you reconnect with joy when nothing feels good? Just like building an exercise routine, rebuilding your connection to joy needs to start small: Begin with tiny doses : Set a timer for 5 minutes to dabble in something you used to enjoy. No pressure to continue after the timer ends. Create a cozy environment : Make your surroundings as comfortable as possible. Soft blankets, good lighting, whatever helps your body feel at ease. Body-brain connection : Regular movement, even just a short walk, can help boost dopamine , which is important for both motivation and feeling good. Sleep support : Our ability to feel pleasure takes a nosedive when we're sleep-deprived. All of our ADHD symptoms suffer , too. Building better sleep habits can help. Connect gently : Message a friend or loved one who gets it - even if all you can manage is an emoji or a meme. Sometimes just knowing you’re not alone can help. 🏥 When should you reach out for help with anhedonia? While anhedonia can improve with self-care steps, sometimes we need extra support. Consider talking with a healthcare provider if: The emptiness feeling lasts more than a few weeks You're having thoughts of harming yourself Daily tasks feel impossible You're using substances to try to feel more Your sleep or appetite has changed dramatically 📍Finding your way back Living with ADHD means our brains sometimes need different pathways to joy than neurotypical folks. And that's okay! Personally, one of my favorite joyful activities is sitting in the local creek looking for fossils. I’ll do it for hours . There's no one-size-fits-all approach to reconnecting with pleasure, and it's perfectly fine to experiment until you find what works for your unique brain. Remember, seeking support isn't just okay - it's a smart strategy for getting back to feeling like yourself. What tiny step could you take today to reconnect with something you used to enjoy? P.S. If you're struggling with thoughts of self-harm, you're not alone. Call 988 or text 741741 anytime to connect with someone who wants to listen. ‍

body_text: Building What Comes Next in Advertising: Recognized by the BIG Innovation Awards January 16, 2026 in Blog Innovation in advertising is rarely a single moment. More often, it’s the result of years spent building infrastructure, testing assumptions, and making deliberate bets on where the industry is headed—often well before the market is ready. It requires steady execution, technical conviction, and the willingness to build new systems when the industry’s ambitions move faster than its tools. This year, that mindset earned industry recognition for Viant— the Business Intelligence Group named CEO and Co-Founder Tim Vanderhook an Innovative Individual in the 2026 BIG Innovation Awards , AND recognized ViantAI as a winning product in the Internet and Technology category. These two awards tell a single story: leadership that builds, and a product that proves it out in the market. Leadership Grounded in Building Tim Vanderhook has spent more than 25 years building businesses at the intersection of media and technology, with a career defined by identifying structural shifts in how advertising operates and building platforms to support them . He co-founded Viant alongside his brother, Chris Vanderhook , with a focus on building advertising infrastructure that could adapt as the industry changed. Today, Viant operates as a leading independent buy-side platform , helping advertisers reach audiences across channels with a clear focus on performance, accountability, and transparency across the open internet. Over the course of his career, Tim has recognized moments of industry inflection early, and built the platforms that carried the market forward. He helped lay early programmatic foundations and later co-founded XUMO, alongside Chris before streaming and CTV began to reshape television, contributing to one of the earliest large-scale free, ad-supported platforms before FAST became the familiar acronym it is today. A product-driven CEO, he has also remained close to the technical side of the business; Tim holds multiple patents tied to household-based identification and programmatic marketplace design that continue to influence how addressability and measurement function today. That mix of long-range thinking and hands-on execution shows up clearly in the roadmap of ViantAI. Rather than stepping back as the product took shape, Tim personally designed and coded the initial alpha, recognizing AI’s potential to reduce friction and drive more efficient campaign execution at scale. This award from the Business Intelligence Group underscores what sets Tim apart as a leader and visionary in AdTech: the instinct to see what’s coming, the technical fluency to build for it, and the discipline to turn ideas into systems marketers can rely on. ViantAI in Market Alongside Tim’s recognition, ViantAI was also named an Innovative Product in the Internet and Technology category by the Business Intelligence Group . Viant launched this AI suite to address a familiar challenge in digital advertising, where teams spend hours on manual work across planning, execution, and reporting while those functions live in separate, fragmented systems. The result is disconnected tools, constant data reconciliation, and insights that often arrive too late to meaningfully influence performance. ViantAI transforms this process by bridging those workflows in a single, intuitive platform. With just four inputs, marketers can generate omnichannel media plans, activate them directly within the Demand-Side Platform and monitor performance through conversational measurement prompts. Optimization continues throughout the campaign, using Viant’s proprietary data and bid-stream intelligence to maximize efficiency. Since launch, adoption has grown steadily, with ViantAI Bidding automating approximately 85% of all ad spend on the Viant platform. Customers report up to 50% lower media costs, 42% lower CPMs, transforming campaign planning, setup, trafficking, and optimization from days to hours. ViantAI’s recognition by the Business Intelligence Group, alongside recent honors from Adweek and MarTech Breakthrough , reflects a platform that has already crossed an important threshold—AI is no longer an add-on, but embedded infrastructure shaping how campaigns are planned and optimized. Introducing Outcomes At CES 2026 , Viant introduced the next phase of ViantAI with the launch of Outcomes , the industry’s first fully autonomous advertising product built for the open internet. Where ViantAI’s planning, optimization, and measurement tools act as a media co-pilot, Outcomes shifts these capabilities into autopilot, while the platform drives relentlessly toward a defined performance goal for advertisers. Outcomes is powered by Viant’s newly developed AI Lattice Brain , a decisioning architecture designed to run campaigns autonomously while remaining transparent. The system evaluates multiple proprietary signals in parallel, including Viant Household ID, contextual intelligence through IRIS_ID, supply quality, historical performance, and campaign delivery data to guide execution in real time. With Outcomes, advertisers simply define the business result they want to achieve, such as customer acquisition or return on ad spend. ViantAI then manages campaign decisioning and optimization toward that outcome, while still giving teams visibility into where ads run and how performance is delivered—a level of transparency that walled simply cannot offer. That combination of autonomy and transparency is foundational to how Viant approaches AI-driven advertising on the open internet. Outcomes is the natural next chapter for ViantAI. As the platform takes on more decisioning and optimization, its launch marks a clear shift in how advertising is managed, with more responsibility moving into the system and less friction left for marketers to navigate. A Meaningful Marker Moments of recognition like this tend to clarify what’s already in motion. Leadership and product don’t always move in lockstep, but when they do, it’s evident in the work. Over the past year, ViantAI has moved beyond a point solution or roadmap concept, shaping how teams plan, activate, and optimize campaigns. The launch of Outcomes carries that work forward, signaling a platform that continues to evolve rather than pause at milestones. Viant’s focus remains squarely on what comes next: continuing to build advertising technology that delivers meaningful, frictionless outcomes for marketers as the industry moves forward. Winners are selected by a panel of experienced business leaders and practitioners, with a focus on progress that goes beyond buzzwords and delivers tangible results. As Russ Fordyce, Chief Recognition Officer at the Business Intelligence Group, noted: “True innovation is no longer about chasing the latest buzzwords. Expand A cookieless DSP is a programmatic advertising platform that identifies and reaches audiences using durable, privacy-first identifiers rather than third-party cookies. Instead of relying on fragile browser tracking, these platforms leverage advanced solutions like Household ID™ to maintain scale and precision. This approach ensures that digital campaigns remain effective and measurable regardless of evolving browser restrictions or privacy regulations. How does programmatic advertising work without cookies? Expand Programmatic advertising functions without cookies by activating first-party data through identity resolution frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 and the Household ID. Marketers also utilize contextual targeting to align ads with real-time content and prioritize natively cookieless channels such as CTV and DOOH. These methods allow for high-impact reach and frequency management without the need for invasive user-level tracking. What is the difference between a DSP and a cookieless DSP? Expand Traditional DSPs rely on syncing third-party cookies across exchanges to build audience profiles, a process that is increasingly fragmented and unreliable. A cookieless DSP uses people-based identity, first-party data, and privacy-safe signals to reach consumers across all devices. Viant DSP was purpose-built to be cookieless from the ground up, ensuring it never relied on the legacy infrastructure of third-party cookies. What targeting options are available in a cookieless environment? Expand Marketers in a cookieless environment can utilize a robust suite of options including contextual targeting, first-party data onboarding, and household-level identity resolution. Furthermore, interoperability with alternative ID frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 allows brands to maintain significant scale across the open web. These diverse tactics provide a durable, privacy-forward alternative to outdated cookie-based audience segments. How is campaign performance measured in a cookieless world? Expand In a cookieless world, campaign measurement is achieved through modern attribution models such as incrementality testing, Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), and secure data clean rooms. The Household ID serves as a critical cross-device attribution layer, linking high-impact exposures on CTV to conversions on other digital devices within the home. This transition allows advertisers to prove ROI and optimize spend without relying on fragmented, cookie-based signals. (“Gran Tierra” or the “Company”) (NYSE American:GTE)(TSX:GTE)(LSE:GTE) today provided an operational update. All dollar amounts are in United States dollars and all production volumes are on a working interest before royalties basis and are expressed in barrels of oil equivalent ( “boe” ) per day ( “boepd” ), unless otherwise stated. Operations Update December 2025 Average Production: The Company’s achieved a total Company average production of 48,235 boepd for the month of December, 2025 – the highest monthly production achieved in Company history. Ecuador Production : During the fourth quarter of 2025, Gran Tierra achieved a daily production rate of 10,000 bopd in Ecuador. Current production1 rates are approximately 8,800 barrels of oil per day (“ bopd ”). Fulfilled Ecuador Exploration Commitments: All Ecuador exploration commitments have been finalized, highlighted by successful discoveries at Conejo in the Hollín and Basal Tena sands, which together delivered combined IP60 rates of approximately 3,238 bopd. Conejo A-1 and A-2 Wells: The two Conejo wells continue to produce1 roughly 2,700 barrels of oil per day. Both discoveries added drilling locations. IP60 production rates from A1 and A2 are 1,921 and 1,317 bopd respectively. Field Development Plans (“FDP”) : In the first quarter of 2026, the Iguana FDP was approved. The Chanangue FDP received approval in the third quarter of 2025, while the Charapa and Conejo FDPs were formally submitted in fourth quarter of 2025 and remain under review. In addition, the Perico and Espejo FDPs associated with the previously announced acquisition, have been submitted and are currently undergoing the regulatory review process. Perico and Iguana Field : The Perico field has now been fully integrated into our portfolio with optimizations being developed to capture synergies as we move into 2026 – these include projects such as gas to power, waterflood initiation and operational optimizations. Waterflood: Gran Tierra continues to advance it waterflood development program in line with the approved field development plan. A successful injectivity test in the Basal Tena in the Chanangue field was completed, a key technical milestone supporting the water injection pilot. Construction of the associated water treatment and injection facilities is progressing, targeting an early 2026 injection start. In parallel, the Company plans a second injector conversion in the Basal Tena at Chanangue in the second quarter of 2026, alongside additional injector conversions in the Lower U at the Iguana and Perico fields in second quarter and third quarter 2026, respectively. During the fourth quarter of 2025, gross production at Cohembi increased to approximately 9,100 bopd, driven by the successful delivery of the Raju-1 well and a strong response from the ongoing waterflood program in the northern portion of the field. As a follow-up, the Company plans to drill four gross development wells in Cohembi during the First Half of 2026. The Company expects its capital carry commitments to be completed by mid-2026, after which working interest and cost sharing will revert to standard terms, improving Gran Tierra’s cash netbacks and capital efficiency on future activity. Investors are cautioned that these measures should not be construed as alternatives to oil and natural gas sales, net income or loss or other measures of financial performance as determined in accordance with GAAP. Gran Tierra’s method of calculating these measures may differ from other companies and, accordingly, they may not be comparable to similar measures used by other companies. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as EBITDA (defined as net income or loss adjusted for DD&A expenses, interest expense and income tax expense or recovery) adjusted for non-cash lease expense, lease payments, foreign exchange loss (gain), stock-based compensation expenses or recovery, transaction costs, other loss and unrealized derivative instruments loss (gain). Management uses this supplemental measure to analyze performance and income generated by our principal business activities prior to the consideration of how non-cash items affect that income, and believes that this financial measure is useful supplemental information for investors to analyze our performance and our financial results. A reconciliation from net income to Adjusted EBITDA is not available due to certain components of net income, including taxes and gain on debt securities, not being reasonably estimable at this time. Net debt, as presented, is defined as Gran Tierra’s senior notes and borrowings under Gran Tierra’s credit facility, less cash and cash equivalents. Management believes that net debt is a useful supplemental measure for management and investors in order to evaluate the financial sustainability of the Company’s business and leverage. A reconciliation from total debt to Net Debt is not available due to certain components of our total debt not being reasonably estimable at this time. Operating netback, as presented, is defined as gross profit less depletion and accretion related to producing assets. Management believes that operating netback is a useful supplemental measure for management and investors to analyze financial performance and provides an indication of the results generated by our principal business activities prior to the consideration of other income and expenses.
